messages:
Tara: Quickstart hero variants ready for a quick pass — want a11y + copy + eng sanity check before we lock. Two prototypes: Variant A is a single wide hero with a prominent CTA and animated sample app; Variant B is a compact sticky sample-projects rail below the header that persists as you explore. Link: https://figma.redwood/quickstart-variants (comment pins)
Eli: Love both. A: good for first impression, but might be heavy on visual noise. B: better for discoverability of sample repos. Concern: focus order when the rail appears on keyboard navigation.
Juno: Copy quick notes — current CTA text is `Create API key` which feels slightly technical. Suggest `Generate API key` or `Get started with an API key` for tone. Also for sample project cards, use consistent verbs: "Try demo", "Clone repo", "Open in console" (not mixed).
Maria: Flow-wise, we should ensure the hero variant still surfaces the minimal setup checklist (3 steps) without requiring scroll. Many signups drop off before step 2. Consider a compact checklist pill in A and a sticky floating button in B that opens the checklist panel.
Sam: Implementation notes: Variant A would need the animated preview (lottie?) and the hero should be server-side rendered for perf. Variant B is mostly client-rendered but needs sticky repositioning — tricky for small screens. Also: we need to avoid focus traps when the rail mounts/unmounts.
Anil: Accessibility nits from quick pass: screen reader reads hero image alt text before headline on A — we should set `aria-hidden=\"true\"` on decorative previews and ensure H1 is first in DOM. For B: the rail toggles content that isn't announced; add an `aria-live=\"polite\"` region for new sample project notifications. Also test with zoom 200% and keyboard-only.
AriaBot: Automated a11y scan (axe) summary for Variant A (draft):
- color-contrast: 1 minor (CTA on patterned bg)
- aria-required: 0
- heading-order: 1 (img above H1)
Recommendation: fix heading order, ensure alt/aria-hidden.

AriaBot: Axe report gist: https://internal-reports/axe/1765509876
Sam: Quick code snippet to avoid focus trap when rail mounts — use inert on the underlying container until mount animation completes:
```js
// when rail opens
document.getElementById('main-content').inert = true;
rail.addEventListener('animationend', () => {
  document.getElementById('main-content').inert = false;
  rail.querySelector('button').focus();
});
```
Note: `inert` polyfill required for Safari.
Eli: Design decision: make the checklist pill persistent in both variants. Visual treatment: subtle border + progress dot (1/3). Also add a skip link at top: `Skip onboarding` for returning users — visible on focus.
Juno: Copy suggestion for checklist steps: "1) Generate API key — copy & save\n2) Run the sample app — paste key\n3) Inspect tokens & costs" — shorter microcopy under each step: verbs first.
Tara: Risk/costs — A might increase first-load bytes by ~80KB for animations; B slightly more JS runtime. Which one is higher priority to prototype? My vote: build B first (sticky samples) since it surfaces more real projects and reduces images.
Sam: Agreed on B-first. I'll prototype sticky rail with lazy-loaded images and ensure keyboard order. ETA: PR by EOD Friday.
Anil: I'll run manual screen reader pass on the PR + regression test for zoom and keyboard. Can we add acceptance criteria in the ticket? (a11y checklist + performance budget)
Tara: Yes — I'll update the ticket with acceptance criteria: 1) H1 first in DOM, 2) no focus trap, 3) aria-live for rail announcements, 4) CTA contrast >= 4.5:1, 5) JS payload delta <100KB. Tagging @Sam @Eli @Juno for review.
Eli: Tiny UI copy nit: change sample card footer from "Open" to "Open in Console" for clarity.
Juno: Also recommend a tooltip on the API key step: "This key can be rotated later from Settings" — reduces fear.
Tara: Great. Next steps: Sam protos B + adds inert/polyfill, Anil test, Juno copy pass, Eli visual polish. Meeting quick sync Wednesday 9:30am if we need to unblock.
Sam: Noted. I'll drop a draft PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
Anil: Thanks — will check once PR lands.
